added_failures_note: Both arms of the review-round gate ran the same two files. round3-base-suite.log reads '54 passed in 31.89s' EXIT=0 at revision e595f9f236, and round3-head-suite.log reads '58 passed in 49.65s' EXIT=0 at revision 274c671e4f, so the round adds four cases and no failure; both logs name their revision, tree, resolved module and command on their header lines and end with a bare EXIT= line. The three round3 negative-control logs each record a non-zero exit and a failing test id: refusal '2 failed, 5 passed', double-unescape '1 failed, 6 passed', aggregate-alone '1 failed, 6 passed'.

findings.text: The fail-closed answer now also covers a row the aggregate carries with no document beside it, so a differing narrative on that shape raises the refusal again. That shape is not merely a disagreement: reckon/crew/promotion.py:1246-1249 reaches the aggregate ledger file as the run's record precisely because no run document exists, and reckon/ledger.py:1772 load() returns such a row as this run's history, so the same promotion path now reports the row as present to the refusal reporter at promotion.py:1254 and as not proven to the narrative branch. The base revision answered True for this shape, so a project whose runs were never split out by _split_project_runs regains the double refusal this node exists to remove. No case drives crew.complete for an aggregate-only row, so the narrowed answer on that shape is untested.
